claims.text: Deliberately changing elemental ratios in non-equiatomic HEAs can tune their magnetic transitions and magnetocaloric response.
Ti promotes antiferromagnetic coupling with Fe, Co, and Ni.
Increasing Ti or otherwise departing from equiatomic composition reduces saturation magnetization.
Non-equiatomic compositional tuning enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Changes in composition shift the magnetic ordering or Curie temperatures.
Increasing Ti or reducing saturation magnetization increases coercivity.
The coercive field follows an inverse relationship with saturation magnetization, Hc ∝ 1/Ms.
Shifting magnetic ordering changes the magnetic-entropy change near the transition temperature.
Composition tuning can optimize the magnetocaloric effect, potentially producing a larger isothermal magnetic-entropy change at a targeted transition temperature.
FeCoNiTi-based alloys can contain an fcc component or mixed fcc/C14 phase constitution in the as-cast state.
A non-equiatomic Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy variant exists with composition Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 and is C14-dominant.
Relevant magnetic measurements span approximately 50–1150 K.
The cited FeCoNiTi experiments were conducted on low-dimensional forms such as thin films or nanowires using SQUID magnetometry.
Composition changes modify chemical short-range order and phase fractions in the fcc or mixed-phase region.
Modified short-range order and phase fractions alter local magnetic anisotropy and exchange interactions.
Equiatomic FeCoNiTi exhibits multiple ferromagnetic transitions associated with its fcc and C14 phases.
Equiatomic HEAs generally have relatively high saturation magnetization and lower coercivity.
Composition-tuning effects are most prominent in low-dimensional samples where exchange interactions and anisotropy strongly interplay.
Extreme composition deviations may cause phase separation or loss of the intended magnetic order.
The quantitative composition-property relationship remains uncertain and may depend on processing, sample geometry, and microstructure.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as already non-equiatomic, whereas the intervention is framed as moving away from an equiatomic composition. It is therefore unclear whether the experimental baseline is equiatomic or non-equiatomic.
The baseline broadly characterizes equiatomic HEAs as having lower coercivity, but the cited equiatomic FeCoNiTi system is specifically presented as having a high coercive field in its fcc phase.
